title: Right-sized safety friction cleanup
summary: Reduce WebView safety friction by replacing repeated read-only mutation-boundary paragraphs with concise shared cues, demoting read-only Settings and Launch proof-only blocked styling to review, and leaving deeper pending-drain/network lifecycle behavior unchanged after investigation.
reason: The right-sized safety audit found that read-only evidence panels repeated mutation-level language even though backend routes, strict confirmations, command journaling, and manifest-backed publish controls already own the real hazards.
behavior_before: Pending Publish, Completed, Queue, Rename, Settings, and Launch proof-only read-only panels repeated long guardrail copy or styled advisory safety evidence as blocked even when no backend route was being rejected.
behavior_after: Read-only WebView panels use shorter shared boundary cues while preserving backend ownership messaging. Settings safety-lock advisory rows and Launch sample-validation proof-only gaps now render as review/warning rather than hard-stop blocked states. Pending drain execution, Network lifecycle dry-run/confirmation gates, command journal requirements, and close-readiness hard stops are unchanged.

rollback_plan: Restore the previous repeated WebView guardrail strings plus Settings safety-lock and Launch proof-only blocked-row styling in the touched assets, revert the matching static/browser smoke expectation updates, refresh generated summaries for the reverted files, and rerun the same targeted WebView/backend validation commands. No media or runtime state migration is required.
